arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: The state argues police had probable cause to believe evidence was in the home.
The state argues the officer secured the home to prevent destruction of evidence.
The state argues the partner went to a judge to get a warrant.
The homeowner argues the police action constituted an unlawful seizure of the home.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The dispute centers on whether police can temporarily block a home to preserve evidence while obtaining a warrant. The state claims this action was necessary and lawful. The homeowner claims this action violated his constitutional rights.

paragraphs: This case defines the limits of police power to secure homes. It determines when officers can block entry to preserve evidence. It balances public safety against individual privacy rights.
